title: Competency‑anchored interview lattice + 8‑week onramp (engineer hires)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook to: (1) standardize how we map hiring signals to discrete competencies (the 'lattice'), (2) provide a short interview choreography + scoring anchors for IC engineer roles, and (3) define a pragmatic 8-week onramp broken into micro-sprints so hiring managers and mentors have a repeatable template.

Audience:
People Ops, hiring managers, interviewers (eng/infra/serving-runtime), hiring committee reviewers, hiring coordinators.

Quick notes / constraints (WIP):
- Goal: reduce time-to-decision and improve post-hire ramp consistency.
- Target roles: Mid SDE (IC2/IC3), Senior SDE (IC4), with optional variant for infra/platform engineers.
- This is intentionally lean: avoid >10 interviewers, prioritize signal over completeness.
- TODO: map to leveling doc + score mapping for managers (action: Priya).

1) Competency lattice (core competencies + 1–4 score anchors)
- System Design (scale & tradeoffs)
  - 1: Basic components and API-level thinking; can propose simple system but misses scaling concerns.
  - 2: Describes service boundaries, caching, basic cost tradeoffs; limited depth on bottlenecks.
  - 3: Clear design with reasoning about latency/throughput, capacity planning, and failure modes.
  - 4: Proposes operational design, migration/rollout plans, and quantifies TL;DR tradeoffs.
- Coding (correctness & clarity)
  - 1: Writes syntactically correct snippets for simple problems; needs heavy guidance.
  - 2: Correct solution for medium problems; reasonable test-thinking.
  - 3: Clean, efficient code; edge-case handling and test approach.
  - 4: Elegant solutions, complexity-optimized, and advocates maintainability patterns.
- Debugging & Postmortem Thinking
  - 1: Can reproduce a bug with help.
  - 2: Explains root cause for common infra bugs, proposes fixes.
  - 3: Drives RCA with hypothesis-driven debug plan and mitigations.
  - 4: Designs instrumentation, rolling mitigations, and long-term prevention.
- Collaboration & Communication
  - 1: Participates in discussions, needs feedback to clarify ideas.
  - 2: Communicates clearly in small groups; documents decisions.
  - 3: Leads cross-team conversations, aligns stakeholders.
  - 4: Influences org decisions; written comms are used as references.
- Ownership & Delivery
  - 1: Delivers small tasks with guidance.
  - 2: Owns features end-to-end with some coaching.
  - 3: Drives multi-week deliveries, handles external dependencies.
  - 4: Shapes roadmap, mentors others on delivery practices.

Scoring guidance (interviewer cheat-sheet):
- Use 1..4 per competency. Average across competencies -> preliminary hire recommendation.
- Flag any 1 in a "must-have" competency (role-dependent) as a potential fail.
- Interviewers must add 1–3 sentence evidence for each low/high score.

2) Interview choreography (60–75m default; 4–5 interviews total)
- Coordinator: send role-level expectations + sample problem a day before (short).
- Suggested panel (example for Mid SDE):
  - 10m: Intro / culture fit (hiring manager) — 1x
  - 30m: Coding (pairing; 1 interviewer) — 1x
  - 25m: System design / architecture (1x) OR debugging exercise depending on candidate background
  - 20m: Collaboration & delivery / behavioral (1x)
  - 10m: Q&A + close (hiring manager)
- Senior hires: add 1x cross-team leadership conversation (30m) focused on tradeoffs, metrics, and rollouts.
- Notes: keep coding problem scoped; prefer live-coding + thought process. For take-home preference: provide 48–72h window and judge on design + tests.

Interview script snippets & probes (drop-in)
- System design: "Design a KV store for session tokens used by our hosted API—how do you ensure low latency and safe eviction under bursty traffic?"
- Debugging: "We see 2x latency spikes on tail tokens during long requests. Walk me through hypotheses and what telemetry you'd fetch."
- Coding: "Implement a rate limiter (token-bucket) with windowed counters; include tests for concurrency edge cases."
- Collaboration: "Tell me about a time you disagreed with product on a rollout approach. How did you escalate and resolve it?"

3) Interview scorecard template (one-line)
- Candidate name | Role | Panel date | System design (1–4) | Coding (1–4) | Debugging (1–4) | Collaboration (1–4) | Ownership (1–4) | Evidence summary | Recommendation (strong/recommend/weak/no)

Calibration notes for interviewers (quick):
- Use concrete evidence — "wrote X algorithm" is weak; "described tradeoff X and measured Y" is strong.
- Resist contrast bias: compare to rubric anchors, not other candidates.
- If uncertain, mark as "needs follow-up" and request a 20m calibration call with hiring manager.

4) 8-week onramp (micro-sprints) — manager + mentor checklist
Overview: 8-week plan split into 4 two-week micro-sprints. Each sprint has clear outcomes, required access, and sample tasks. This is a template; hiring manager should customize.

Week 0 (pre-day1)
- Access: workspace, email, ticketing, repo access, infra VPN, credentials for staging.
- Paperwork: benefits, payroll, NDAs.
- Slack intro + 1-pager from manager: top priorities, team norms, expectations.

Sprint 1 (weeks 1–2) — Orientation & small wins
- Objectives: set up local dev env; run test suite; ship first small bug or doc improvement.
- Checkpoints: daily 1:1 quick sync first week; mentor pairing scheduled.
- Deliverable: PR merged that fixes a low-risk bug + short PR description template.
- Support: onboarding checklist link, stack overview, architecture one-pager.

Sprint 2 (weeks 3–4) — Deeper system knowledge + small feature
- Objectives: own a small feature or backlog item end-to-end in staging.
- Activities: attend architecture review; read relevant RFCs; shadow on-call once with mentor.
- Deliverable: feature branch merged to staging + rollout checklist completed.

Sprint 3 (weeks 5–6) — Ownership & metrics
- Objectives: take ownership of a component area (bug triage, dashboard) and deliver a measurable improvement.
- Activities: define success metric (latency, error rate, deploy frequency), run A/B rollback plan.
- Deliverable: post-merge verification + short postmortem for rollout.

Sprint 4 (weeks 7–8) — Operating independently
- Objectives: lead a small cross-functional change; present learnings to team.
- Activities: propose a small optimization (caching config, batching tweak), measure before/after.
- Deliverable: demo + 1-page runbook for the owned piece.

Manager check-ins / success signals
- Week 2: can reproduce local build and shipped first PR.
- Week 4: accepted feature on staging; demonstrates reading of system docs.
- Week 6: drives an incident postmortem or metric-improvement plan.
- Week 8: independently triages and leads a small rollout.

Fail-fast signals (early remediation)
- Still cannot run tests or get basic access by end of week 1 -> escalate to IT + People Ops.
- Lack of collaboration evidence by week 4 -> mentorship intensification + formal improvement plan.

Onboarding artifacts to create per hire (template list)
- 1-page "ownership canvas" for direct report (manager fills in week 1)
- Mentor pairing note with 4x 30m meeting blocks scheduled
- First-30-day learning checklist (repo links, RFC list, monitoring dashboards)
- Access matrix confirmation (security/compliance sign-off for private deployments roles)

Open questions / next steps (WIP)
- How do we map this lattice to compensation bands? Proposal: create a mapping doc after 10 hires for signal validation (action: Ben).
- Can we author a short interviewer training slide deck (15m) + calibration video? (action: Miguel)
- Need to instrument hiring outcomes: add tags to ATS and track 90-day retention + performance signals.

Appendix: short example evidence snippet (good vs bad)
- Bad: "Candidate knows system design. Gave a reasonable answer."
- Good: "Candidate proposed sharding by customer, recommended consistent hashing to reduce rebalancing by ~70%, and suggested a read replica strategy with expected 2x read throughput at 25% cost increase; provided rollout plan with canary and metric checks (95th latency, error rate)."

This doc is an iterative working artifact — expect edits. Use the linked artifacts to pull templates and update calibration notes after each hiring cycle.

-- End of draft --
